# BayesianBenter

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/USERNAME/BayesianBenter/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/USERNAME/BayesianBenter/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**BayesianBenter** provides closed-form Gibbs samplers for Bayesian inference
in the **Benter (1994)** model for ranking data. The Benter model generalizes
Plackett-Luce by adding stage-specific *dampening* exponents
$\alpha_r \in (0, 1]$ that down-weight the information in later ranking stages:

$$
p(\pi_i \mid \lambda, \alpha) = \prod_{r=1}^{J-1}
  \frac{\lambda_{w_{ir}}^{\alpha_r}}{\sum_{j \in R_{ir}} \lambda_j^{\alpha_r}}.
$$

Estimation uses a positive-stable frailty data augmentation that restores
conjugacy: the item worths $\lambda$ are drawn exactly from Gamma full
conditionals, and each dampening exponent $\alpha_r$ is updated by
Metropolis-Hastings on its collapsed conditional. Both **complete** and
**partial (top-$R$)** rankings are supported through a single entry point.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("USERNAME/BayesianBenter")
```

## Usage

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(BayesianBenter)

set.seed(1)
lambda <- c(5, 3, 2, 1.5, 1)
lambda <- lambda / sum(lambda)
alpha  <- c(1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.3)

# simulate 500 complete rankings of J = 5 items
pi <- rBenter(500, lambda, alpha)

# fit the model
fit <- gibbsBenter(pi, J = 5, a = 1, b = 1, c = 1, d = 1,
                   iters = 3000, burnin = 0.5)

rbind(truth = lambda, posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$lambda))
rbind(truth = alpha,  posterior_mean = colMeans(fit$alpha))
```

Partial rankings are passed the same way: leave unranked positions as `NA`
(or supply fewer than `J` columns) and `gibbsBenter()` routes them to the
partial-ranking sampler automatically. Only the dampening parameters up to the
deepest observed rank are estimated; the rest are returned as `NA`.

## References

Benter, W. (1994). Computer-based horse race handicapping and wagering
systems: A report. In *Efficiency of Racetrack Betting Markets*.
